# Preserve credential-storage guarantees when selecting an OH backend

## Platform difference

Availability of a preferences or encryption-shaped API does not establish equivalent protected credential storage on OH.

## Implementation

SSH Codex introduces an explicit SecureKeyValueStore dispatch between Android and OH, and Bugaoshan separately selects its OH secure-storage package. Enjoy Plus stores tokens in ordinary SharedPreferences; Nomark persists session/cookie keys in native preferences. Minecraft Box reaches a constant device-ID fallback on OH and derives deterministic encryption material, with a plaintext-on-error path. Xingmu's unused in-memory keyring module carries an AES label but implements XOR/Base64; it is a negative example, not an OH restriction.

## Applicability

Use the platform implementation whose security properties meet the app's requirements, and audit those properties separately. The reviewed secure-storage package selection is not an audit of its cryptography.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Never generalize these application shortcuts into required HarmonyOS behavior. The Xingmu study found no construction outside the module, so no claim is made that active credentials pass through it. Preserve distinctions between session convenience storage and secrets.

## Verification

Test persistence and deletion, unavailable backend/error paths, access after restart and application reinstall policy; inspect the actual protected-storage mechanism rather than trusting class or algorithm names.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.

Toki OH discovery: Do not endorse this crypto implementation as secure or usable. Source assumes first 16 output bytes form IV and passes HUKS_TAG_IV on decrypt; no explicit GCM AE tag extraction is present, key generation catches all errors, and missing/read/authentication failure are conflated in Dart. Primary protocol comparison: https://github.com/openharmony/docs/blob/master/en/application-dev/security/UniversalKeystoreKit/huks-encryption-decryption-arkts.md describes NONCE and AEAD requirements and shows HUKS_TAG_NONCE/HUKS_TAG_AE_TAG.
